labs.title: Create and publish a finance sensitivity label in Microsoft Purview
labs.summary: Use a simulated Microsoft Purview portal to create a sensitivity label with encryption and content marking, then publish it only to Finance.
labs.scenario: Contoso's finance team handles budget workbooks and vendor payment email. In the **simulated Microsoft Purview portal** on your lab VM, create a sensitivity label named **Confidential - Finance** that applies to **Files & other data assets** and **Emails**. Configure it to encrypt content for the **Finance group** with **Co-Author** permissions, add the header **CONFIDENTIAL - FINANCE**, and recommend the label when a **Credit Card Number** is detected. Then publish the label in a label policy scoped to Finance, requiring labels and justification when users remove or lower a label.
learningObjectives: Create a Microsoft Purview sensitivity label for files and email
Configure label protection, visual markings, and auto-labeling recommendations
Publish a label policy to a targeted group with required labeling and downgrade justification
prerequisites: Know that sensitivity labels classify and protect data, while retention labels manage lifecycle and deletion.

steps.title: Open Sensitivity labels
steps.instruction: In the portal menu, select **Sensitivity labels**, then select **+ Create**.
steps.hint: Sensitivity labels are under Solutions > Information Protection.
steps.explanation: Sensitivity labels are created before they can be published to users.

steps.title: Name the label and choose scope
steps.instruction: Set **Name** and **Display name** to **Confidential - Finance**. For scope, select **Files & other data assets** and **Emails** only.
steps.hint: Groups & sites is for containers; Meetings is not needed here.
steps.explanation: Scope controls where the label appears and which settings pages are relevant.

rules.description: Confidential - Finance exists for files and email only
rules.failureFeedback: Create the label with Files & other data assets and Emails selected.

steps.title: Configure protection and marking
steps.instruction: Turn on **Control access**, assign permissions to **Finance group** with **Co-Author**, turn on **Apply content marking**, and set **Header text** to **CONFIDENTIAL - FINANCE**.
steps.hint: Encryption controls access; content marking makes the classification visible.
steps.explanation: A label can classify, protect, and apply visual markings.

rules.description: Label has encryption for Finance and visible marking
rules.failureFeedback: Use Finance group, Co-Author, Control access, and the exact header.

steps.title: Add an auto-labeling recommendation
steps.instruction: Turn on **Recommend this label automatically** and choose **Credit Card Number**. Then select **Review and finish** and **Create label**.
steps.hint: A recommendation prompts users; publishing still controls who receives the label.
steps.explanation: Sensitive information types help recommend labels when matching content is detected.

steps.title: Start a publishing policy
steps.instruction: Open **Publishing policies**, select **Publish label**, and choose **Confidential - Finance**.
steps.hint: Publishing policies make labels visible to selected users and apply policy settings.
steps.explanation: Creating a label does not make it available in apps until it is added to a label policy.

rules.failureFeedback: Create a publishing policy that includes Confidential - Finance.

steps.title: Scope and configure the policy
steps.instruction: Keep **Full directory**, publish to **Finance group** only, require downgrade justification, require users to apply labels to email and documents, set **Confidential - Finance** as default, name the policy, and select **Submit**.
steps.explanation: Policy scope decides who receives the label and settings.

rules.description: Policy is scoped to Finance and requires labels
rules.failureFeedback: Publish only to Finance and enable required label plus justification.

labs.solution:
1. Select **Sensitivity labels** > **+ Create**.
2. On **Name and description**, enter `Confidential - Finance` for **Name** and **Display name**.
3. On **Define the scope for this label**, select **Files & other data assets** and **Emails** only.
4. On **Choose protection settings**, turn on **Control access**, assign **Finance group** with **Co-Author**, turn on **Apply content marking**, set **Header text** to `CONFIDENTIAL - FINANCE`, turn on **Recommend this label automatically**, and choose **Credit Card Number**.
5. Select **Review and finish** > **Create label**.
6. Go to **Publishing policies** > **Publish label**. Choose **Confidential - Finance**, keep **Full directory**, and publish to **Finance group** only.
7. Turn on downgrade justification, require labels for email and documents, set **Confidential - Finance** as default, name the policy `Publish Confidential - Finance to Finance`, and select **Submit**.
